title: Legal compensation (Belgium)
subtitle: Compensation owed for a total service interruption of 8 hours or more.
legal_basis: Article 113/2 of the Belgian electronic communications act, in force since 1 November 2024.
scope_total_only: This scheme covers a total and continuous interruption only. Degraded throughput, weak Wi-Fi or a partially available service open no right to it.
scope_speed_pointer: For a degradation rather than an outage, see the mediation module: the route is a complaint, not this scale.
clock_note: The legal clock starts when the operator becomes aware of the interruption -- notification to the BIPT, or the first report by a user. Not when your line went down. Report an outage to support immediately, even when it looks obvious.
none_found: No interruption reaching 8 hours in this window.
not_qualified: Observed duration, not the legal duration: enter the time you reported the outage to compute what is actually owed.
result_below: Below the 8-hour threshold: no compensation under this scheme.
result_force_majeure: No compensation is owed for an interruption caused by force majeure.
floor_applied: Floor applied: one thirtieth of the monthly fee exceeds the scale.
verify: Amounts and conditions must be verified against the BIPT page before they go into a letter.
index_hint: The legal amounts are indexed each year on the consumer price index. Without a factor, Mire shows the 2024 amounts, which are a floor rather than what is owed.
not_indexed: Amount not indexed: at least this, based on the {year} scale.
exclusion.customer_equipment: Equipment outside the public network (modem, set-top box, SIM, repeater)
exclusion.alternative_accepted: An alternative solution was offered and accepted
result_excluded: No compensation is owed for this cause.
threshold_note: The 8-hour threshold is the one in force. The BIPT has put a revision to 12 hours out for consultation; it is a proposal, not current law.
settings_desc: Monthly fee and indexation used to compute what is owed.
monthly_fee_hint: The fee you actually pay for the interrupted service, or the whole bundle if it is part of one. It drives the floor, which decides the amount in most cases.
floor_note: The scale and the floor coexist: whichever is higher applies. On a 60 EUR subscription the floor is 2 EUR, which the scale only exceeds beyond four days of interruption. The floor is computed on the fee you enter, so it is always current -- indexation only affects the scale.
automatic_note: On a post-paid subscription the compensation is owed automatically: the operator must pay it without you asking. Only prepaid cards require a claim. Reporting the outage remains in your interest, since it starts the legal clock.
